question: A 15-year-old Indian adolescent boy has a BMI of 23 kg/m² (at the 75th centile for age) and a waist circumference of 82 cm. His fasting blood glucose is 98 mg/dL and blood pressure is 126/80 mmHg. Which statement regarding his NCD risk is MOST accurate?

answers.text: His BMI is within the normal range for age, so metabolic screening is not indicated.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: BMI alone is insufficient for NCD risk assessment in South Asian adolescents. Waist circumference, blood pressure, and glycaemia must also be evaluated. The South Asian paradox means significant metabolic risk can occur at lower BMI.

answers.text: South Asians accumulate visceral adipose tissue at lower BMI than Western populations, so this adolescent may already have significant metabolic risk despite a seemingly normal BMI.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The 'South Asian paradox' refers to higher visceral fat and insulin resistance at equivalent BMI compared to Western populations. Indian adolescents with BMI ≥23 or waist circumference above age-specific cut-offs, combined with borderline BP and fasting glucose, represent high-risk individuals requiring counselling and follow-up.

answers.text: A fasting blood glucose of 98 mg/dL is diagnostic of type 2 diabetes and warrants immediate treatment.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Fasting glucose ≥126 mg/dL (on two occasions) is diagnostic of diabetes. 98 mg/dL is within the normal fasting range (<100 mg/dL). This value requires surveillance, not treatment.

answers.text: Hypertension in adolescents is defined using adult thresholds (≥140/90 mmHg), so this boy's BP of 126/80 is entirely normal.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Adolescent hypertension is defined using age-, sex-, and height-specific percentile tables. A BP at or above the 95th percentile on repeated measurement constitutes hypertension in adolescents. Adult cut-offs do not directly apply until 18 years.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the mechanisms of NCD risk in Indian adolescents. The South Asian paradox means that metabolic disease risk (insulin resistance, dyslipidaemia, hypertension) develops at lower BMI in South Asians. Adolescent BP must be interpreted using age-sex-height percentiles, not adult thresholds.

Correct. The South Asian adiposity paradox is a key concept for Indian clinical practice. NCD risk assessment in adolescents must include BMI-for-age, waist circumference, BP percentile, and fasting glucose — not BMI alone. Early identification enables lifestyle counselling before overt disease.
